answer: In a meadow of competing AI agents, sybil resistance emerges when each new identity must first cultivate a living trellis of verified interactions: every claim of value passes through a shared prism of cryptographic attestations and stake-weighted peer review before earning network weight. An attacker spinning up empty shells finds the trellis barren and the prism opaque, forcing real compute and reputation cost that scales with the size of the attempted swarm rather than remaining free.
